mn96:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Sāvatthi in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park.
mn96:2.1: Then Esukārī the brahmin went to the Blessed One and exchanged greetings with him.
mn96:2.2: When the courteous and amiable talk was finished, he sat down at one side. When he had done so, Esukārī the brahmin said to the Blessed One:
mn96:3.1: “Master Gotama, brahmins prescribe four kinds of service—
mn96:3.2: they prescribe service for the brahmin, service for the noble, service for the merchant, service for the worker.
mn96:3.3: Now this, Master Gotama, is the service for the brahmin that brahmins prescribe:
mn96:3.4: ‘a brahmin may serve a brahmin, a noble may serve a brahmin, a merchant may serve a brahmin, or a worker may serve a brahmin.’
mn96:3.5: This, Master Gotama, is the service for the brahmin that brahmins prescribe.
mn96:3.6: And this, Master Gotama, is the service for the noble that brahmins prescribe:
mn96:3.7: ‘a noble may serve a noble, a merchant may serve a noble, or a worker may serve a noble.’
mn96:3.8: This, Master Gotama, is the service for the noble that brahmins prescribe.
mn96:3.9: And this, Master Gotama, is the service for the merchant that brahmins prescribe:
mn96:3.10: ‘a merchant may serve a merchant, or a worker may serve a merchant.’
mn96:3.11: This, Master Gotama, is the service for the merchant that brahmins prescribe.
mn96:3.12: And this, Master Gotama, is the service for the worker that brahmins prescribe:
mn96:3.13: ‘only a worker may serve a worker;
mn96:3.14: for who else would serve a worker?’
mn96:3.15: This, Master Gotama, is the service for the worker that brahmins prescribe.
mn96:3.16: These, Master Gotama, are the four kinds of service that brahmins prescribe.[^1]
mn96:3.17: What does Master Gotama say about this?”
mn96:4.1: “But, brahmin, does the whole world grant the brahmins permission to prescribe these four kinds of service?”
mn96:4.3: “Suppose, brahmin, there were a poor, penniless, destitute man, and they were to force a piece of meat on him against his will, saying: ‘Good man, you must eat this meat, and you must pay for it.’
mn96:4.4: So too, brahmin, without the consent of those ascetics and brahmins, the brahmins nevertheless prescribe these four kinds of service.[^2]
mn96:5.1: I do not say, brahmin, that everyone should be served; nor do I say, brahmin, that no one should be served.
mn96:5.2: For, brahmin, whoever, by serving someone, would become worse and not better on account of that service, I say that person should not be served;
mn96:5.3: and whoever, by serving someone, would become better and not worse on account of that service, I say that person should be served.
mn96:6.1: If, brahmin, they were to ask a noble thus:
mn96:6.2: ‘Of these two—the one whom, by serving, you would become worse and not better on account of that service, or the one whom, by serving, you would become better and not worse on account of that service—
mn96:6.3: which of these should you serve?’ then, brahmin, a noble, answering rightly, would answer thus:
mn96:6.4: ‘I would not serve him by serving whom, on account of that service, I would become worse and not better; but I would serve him by serving whom, on account of that service, I would become better and not worse.’
mn96:7.1: If, brahmin, they were to ask a brahmin …
mn96:7.2: if they were to ask a merchant …
mn96:7.3: if they were to ask a worker thus:
mn96:7.4: ‘Of these two—the one whom, by serving, you would become worse and not better on account of that service, or the one whom, by serving, you would become better and not worse on account of that service—
mn96:7.5: which of these should you serve?’ then, brahmin, a worker too, answering rightly, would answer thus:
mn96:7.6: ‘I would not serve him by serving whom, on account of that service, I would become worse and not better; but I would serve him by serving whom, on account of that service, I would become better and not worse.’
mn96:7.7: I do not say, brahmin, that a man is better for being of high birth, nor do I say, brahmin, that he is worse for being of high birth;[^3]
mn96:7.8: I do not say, brahmin, that he is better for great beauty, nor do I say, brahmin, that he is worse for great beauty;
mn96:7.9: I do not say, brahmin, that he is better for great wealth, nor do I say, brahmin, that he is worse for great wealth.
mn96:8.1: For, brahmin, one of high birth may be a killer of living beings, a taker of what is not given, one who misconducts himself in sensual desires, a speaker of falsehood, a speaker of malicious speech, a speaker of harsh speech, a gossip, covetous, of ill will, and of wrong view.
mn96:8.2: That is why I say a man is not better for being of high birth.
mn96:8.3: And, brahmin, one of high birth may abstain from killing living beings, from taking what is not given, from misconduct in sensual desires, from false speech, from malicious speech, from harsh speech, from gossip, and be uncovetous, of good will, and of right view.
mn96:8.4: That is why I say a man is not worse for being of high birth.
mn96:8.5: One of great beauty too, brahmin, may be a killer of living beings …
mn96:8.7: one of great wealth too, brahmin, may be a killer of living beings …
mn96:8.10: That is why I say a man is not better for great wealth.
mn96:8.11: And one of great wealth too, brahmin, may abstain from killing living beings … and be of right view.
mn96:8.12: That is why I say a man is not worse for great wealth.
mn96:9.1: I do not say, brahmin, that everyone should be served, nor do I say, brahmin, that no one should be served.
mn96:9.2: For, brahmin, whoever, by serving someone, finds that his faith increases, his virtue increases, his learning increases, his generosity increases, and his wisdom increases, on account of that service—that person, I say, should be served.
mn96:9.3: But whoever, by serving someone, finds that his faith does not increase, his virtue does not increase, his learning does not increase, his generosity does not increase, and his wisdom does not increase, on account of that service—that person, I say, should not be served.”
mn96:10.1: When this was said, Esukārī the brahmin said to the Blessed One:
mn96:10.2: “Master Gotama, brahmins prescribe four kinds of proper wealth—
mn96:10.3: they prescribe the proper wealth for the brahmin, the proper wealth for the noble, the proper wealth for the merchant, and the proper wealth for the worker.
mn96:10.4: Now, Master Gotama, this is the proper wealth for the brahmin that brahmins prescribe: alms-gathering;
mn96:10.5: and a brahmin who scorns his proper wealth of alms-gathering acts wrongly, like a herdsman taking what is not given.[^4]
mn96:10.6: This, Master Gotama, is the proper wealth for the brahmin that brahmins prescribe.
mn96:10.7: And this, Master Gotama, is the proper wealth for the noble that brahmins prescribe: the bow and quiver;
mn96:10.8: and a noble who scorns his proper wealth of the bow and quiver acts wrongly, like a herdsman taking what is not given.
mn96:10.9: This, Master Gotama, is the proper wealth for the noble that brahmins prescribe.
mn96:10.10: And this, Master Gotama, is the proper wealth for the merchant that brahmins prescribe: farming and cattle-raising;
mn96:10.11: and a merchant who scorns his proper wealth of farming and cattle-raising acts wrongly, like a herdsman taking what is not given.
mn96:10.12: This, Master Gotama, is the proper wealth for the merchant that brahmins prescribe.
mn96:10.13: And this, Master Gotama, is the proper wealth for the worker that brahmins prescribe: the sickle and carrying-yoke;[^5]
mn96:10.14: and a worker who scorns his proper wealth of the sickle and carrying-yoke acts wrongly, like a herdsman taking what is not given.
mn96:10.15: This, Master Gotama, is the proper wealth for the worker that brahmins prescribe.
mn96:10.16: These, Master Gotama, are the four kinds of proper wealth that brahmins prescribe.[^6]
mn96:10.17: What does Master Gotama say about this?”
mn96:11.1: “But, brahmin, does the whole world grant the brahmins permission to prescribe these four kinds of proper wealth?”
mn96:11.3: “Suppose, brahmin, there were a poor, penniless, destitute man, and they were to force a piece of meat on him against his will, saying: ‘Good man, you must eat this meat, and you must pay for it.’
mn96:11.4: So too, brahmin, without the consent of those ascetics and brahmins, the brahmins nevertheless prescribe these four kinds of proper wealth.
mn96:12.1: I prescribe the noble, supramundane Dhamma as a man’s own proper wealth.
mn96:12.2: But if one recalls his ancient maternal and paternal lineage, then, in whatever family his individual existence has come to be, he is reckoned accordingly.
mn96:12.3: If his individual existence has come to be in a noble family, he is reckoned as a noble;
mn96:12.4: if his individual existence has come to be in a brahmin family, he is reckoned as a brahmin;
mn96:12.5: if his individual existence has come to be in a merchant family, he is reckoned as a merchant;
mn96:12.6: if his individual existence has come to be in a worker family, he is reckoned as a worker.
mn96:12.7: Just as, brahmin, a fire is reckoned only by the condition dependent on which it burns.
mn96:12.8: If a fire burns dependent on logs, it is reckoned just as a log fire;
mn96:12.9: if a fire burns dependent on chips, it is reckoned just as a chip fire;
mn96:12.10: if a fire burns dependent on grass, it is reckoned just as a grass fire;
mn96:12.11: if a fire burns dependent on cow-dung, it is reckoned just as a cow-dung fire.
mn96:12.12: So too, brahmin, I prescribe the noble, supramundane Dhamma as a man’s own proper wealth.
mn96:12.13: But if one recalls his ancient maternal and paternal lineage, then, in whatever family his individual existence has come to be, he is reckoned accordingly.
mn96:12.14: If his individual existence has come to be in a noble family, he is reckoned as a noble;
mn96:12.15: if his individual existence has come to be in a brahmin family, he is reckoned as a brahmin;
mn96:12.16: if his individual existence has come to be in a merchant family, he is reckoned as a merchant;
mn96:12.17: if his individual existence has come to be in a worker family, he is reckoned as a worker.
mn96:13.1: If, brahmin, one from a noble family has gone forth from the home life into homelessness, and, coming to the Dhamma and Discipline proclaimed by a Tathāgata, abstains from killing living beings, from taking what is not given, from unchastity,[^7] from false speech, from malicious speech, from harsh speech, from gossip, is uncovetous, of good will, and of right view, he has attained success in the true, wholesome Dhamma.
mn96:13.2: If one from a brahmin family has gone forth from the home life into homelessness, brahmin, and, coming to the Dhamma and Discipline proclaimed by a Tathāgata, abstains from killing living beings … is of right view, he has attained success in the true, wholesome Dhamma.
mn96:13.3: If one from a merchant family has gone forth from the home life into homelessness, brahmin, and, coming to the Dhamma and Discipline proclaimed by a Tathāgata, abstains from killing living beings … is of right view, he has attained success in the true, wholesome Dhamma.
mn96:13.4: If one from a worker family has gone forth from the home life into homelessness, brahmin, and, coming to the Dhamma and Discipline proclaimed by a Tathāgata, abstains from killing living beings … is of right view, he has attained success in the true, wholesome Dhamma.
mn96:14.2: is only a brahmin capable of developing a mind of loving-kindness towards this district, free of hostility and ill will, and not a noble, a merchant, or a worker?”
mn96:14.4: A noble too, Master Gotama, is capable of developing a mind of loving-kindness towards this district, free of hostility and ill will;
mn96:14.8: all four castes, Master Gotama, are capable of developing a mind of loving-kindness towards this district, free of hostility and ill will.”

mn96:15.2: is only a brahmin capable of taking a bath-powder and loofah, going to a river, and washing off dust and dirt, and not a noble, a merchant, or a worker?”
mn96:15.4: A noble too, Master Gotama, is capable of taking a bath-powder and loofah, going to a river, and washing off dust and dirt;
mn96:15.8: all four castes, Master Gotama, are capable of taking a bath-powder and loofah, going to a river, and washing off dust and dirt.”

mn96:16.2: suppose a head-anointed noble king here were to gather a hundred men of different births, saying:
mn96:16.3: ‘Come, sirs, let those among you who were born in noble families, brahmin families, or royal families take an upper fire-stick made of sāla wood, or sāla-pine wood, or sandalwood, or lotus wood, and kindle a fire, producing heat;
mn96:16.4: and let those among you who were born in outcaste families, hunter families, bamboo-worker families, cartwright families, or scavenger families take an upper fire-stick made from a dog’s feeding-trough, or a pig’s trough, or a washerman’s trough, or castor-oil wood, and kindle a fire, producing heat.’”
mn96:16.6: would the fire kindled and the heat produced by those born in noble, brahmin, and royal families, using an upper fire-stick made of sāla wood, or sāla-pine wood, or sandalwood, or lotus wood, have a flame, a colour, and a radiance, and would one be able to do with that fire what should be done with fire;
mn96:16.7: while the fire kindled and the heat produced by those born in outcaste, hunter, bamboo-worker, cartwright, and scavenger families, using an upper fire-stick made from a dog’s feeding-trough, a pig’s trough, a washerman’s trough, or castor-oil wood, would have no flame, no colour, and no radiance, and one would not be able to do with that fire what should be done with fire?”
mn96:16.9: The fire kindled and the heat produced by those born in noble, brahmin, and royal families, using an upper fire-stick made of sāla wood, or sāla-pine wood, or sandalwood, or lotus wood, would have a flame, a colour, and a radiance, and one would be able to do with that fire what should be done with fire;
mn96:16.10: and the fire kindled and the heat produced by those born in outcaste, hunter, bamboo-worker, cartwright, and scavenger families, using an upper fire-stick made from a dog’s feeding-trough, a pig’s trough, a washerman’s trough, or castor-oil wood, would likewise have a flame, a colour, and a radiance, and one would be able to do with that fire what should be done with fire.
mn96:16.11: For all fire, Master Gotama, has a flame, a colour, and a radiance, and with any fire one is able to do what should be done with fire.”
mn96:16.12: “So too, brahmin, if one from a noble family has gone forth from the home life into homelessness, and, coming to the Dhamma and Discipline proclaimed by a Tathāgata, abstains from killing living beings … is of right view, he has attained success in the true, wholesome Dhamma.
mn96:16.13: If one from a brahmin family, brahmin …
mn96:16.14: if one from a merchant family, brahmin …
mn96:16.15: if one from a worker family has gone forth from the home life into homelessness, brahmin, and, coming to the Dhamma and Discipline proclaimed by a Tathāgata, abstains from killing living beings, from taking what is not given, from unchastity, from false speech, from malicious speech, from harsh speech, from gossip, is uncovetous, of good will, and of right view, he has attained success in the true, wholesome Dhamma.”
mn96:17.1: When this was said, Esukārī the brahmin said to the Blessed One:
mn96:17.3: Let Master Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone to him for refuge from today for life.”
